Yankton College
background: Private liberal arts college in Yankton, South Dakota, affiliated with the Congregational churches (United Church of Christ); the first institution of higher education in Dakota Territory.
history: Chartered on August 30, 1881 by the Rev. Dr. Joseph Ward, Yankton College was the first institution of higher learning in Dakota Territory and the oldest private college in South Dakota. It grew from a single hall on College Hill into a liberal arts college with a Conservatory of Music, a School of Theology (formed after a 1932 merger with Redfield College) and a Clark astronomical observatory, and it produced nine Rhodes Scholars over its history. Carrying a debt of about $1 million and depleted endowments, its trustees announced on December 17, 1984 that the 103-year-old college would close at the end of that week, and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy; its 240 students had to transfer mid-year. The campus became the Federal Prison Camp, Yankton, in 1988. History adapted from the Yankton College history page and Wikipedia (CC BY-SA).
notes: Closed December 1984 (final day December 21). Cause: financial. At closure the college carried a $526,000 debt from the prior year, projected a further $424,000 deficit for 1984-85, and faced a $120,000 December payroll for 118 full- and part-time employees against $37,000 in its checking account; trustees estimated $2.3 million was needed to keep it open, and filed Chapter 11 (Yankton Press & Dakotan, 'Closure Of YC Ended An Era,' Sep 14 1999). Congregational/UCC affiliation and 1988 conversion to Federal Prison Camp, Yankton per Wikipedia. Nine Rhodes Scholars per the Rhodes Trust winners-by-institution list.
